title: Night shift at Kiln Ferry
summary: Two people run the night shift at Kiln Ferry dock. A vendor demo can name damaged parcels on a bench. The feeder circuit cannot carry that demo through the shift.

bullets: On 20 Oct 2026 Chamath Palihapitiya said he thinks AGI is here and that it cannot diffuse because the build-out is missing.
That sentence is his judgement. It does not define AGI and it is not a demonstrated capability.

grounding:
## Technology
- **emTech:** ai
- **Product category:** Shift-scale vision and drafting assist for a parcel dock

## Capabilities
A current vision model can flag a torn parcel, a missing label, or a stack that leans, when the camera sees the bench and a person checks the flag. A drafting assist can suggest the next bin. The check stays with the person on the shift.

## Trends & predictions
Cameras and on-site models get cheaper. Power and a human checker still bound a night dock. A guest's forecast is an opinion. It is not what this shift proves.

## Milestone
Bench demos in 2026 can name visible damage on a parcel in good light. That is a bench, not a staffed night.

## Honest limits
The dock, the circuit, and the night crew are fictional. Winning this shift does not establish that AGI exists or that build-out is the real world's only bottleneck. Power, physical handling, and responsibility are not granted.

## Unlocks Use Case(s)
Flagging damaged parcels for a person who still decides. A short list of what the shift will not hand to the demo.

## Applications
A night board that shows only the flags a person confirmed. A cart that stops when someone is in the aisle. A paper list for the hour the circuit drops.

mission.scene: Kiln Ferry is a fictional night parcel dock. Two people face damaged parcels and a vendor demo that can name the damage on a lit bench. The feeder circuit drops when the belt and the demo run together. The morning truck still expects a clean count.
mission.briefMd:
## The place

Two people keep the night at Kiln Ferry, an inland parcel dock. The belt coughs. One feeder circuit feeds the lights, the belt, and a bench where a vendor demo can name a torn parcel.

The demo works on that bench. It does not work as the shift. When the belt is up, the circuit drops. The morning truck still wants a count.

## The bigger problem

A tool can look finished on a bench and still be impossible to run where the work is. The constraint is the build-out: power, a checker, and a shift that can keep going when the demo stops.

## Your job

Get the night's parcels ready for the morning truck without leaving the crew to absorb unsafe work or uncheckable decisions.
